22cc237_1, 22cc237_2, 29caf6f_1, 3c13f5a_3: the generic file-editing system prompt/tools were injected into AppWorld runs, causing filesystem detours and exposing internal files such as appworld-connection.json and the world socket.

29caf6f_2: generation terminated with output budget exhausted at output_tokens=8192, reasoning_tokens=8192 before any state-changing or supervisor completion call.

manifest.root_cause: The harness's AppWorld execution contract was ambiguous: the sandbox pre-injects `apis`/`requester` as globals but rejects `import apis`, while the system/tool prompt did not say so; generic file-editing tools were attached to AppWorld runs and exposed internal files; tool output was unbounded so API-doc dumps exhausted context; login-token propagation was never stated; and the reasoning-model max_tokens budget was too small to finish viable rollouts.
manifest.targeted_fix: Document the pre-injected AppWorld globals and stateless token semantics in the system and tool prompts; stop attaching file-editing tools and the editing prompt to AppWorld runs; parse, cap, and annotate appworld_execute output with actionable import-denial hints and task_completed; and raise the max_tokens floor for reasoning models so generation budget is not exhausted.

manifest.targeted_fix: Execute each top-level AppWorld statement as its own shell operation and truncate per statement so later outputs stay visible; update the tool description to match; expand the system prompt with supervisor completion rules, relative-date grounding, non-recursive/filtered list usage, binary-file fallback, and pre-mutation planning guardrails.

manifest.root_cause: The harness contract said login() returns a bare access_token and to pass the login variable directly, while the documented login schema is an object. failure_evidence: 22cc237_1: only executed call used `import apis`; sandbox returned `Usage of the following module is not allowed: apis.`; run then hit the 30-turn cap with no recovery or supervisor completion.
29caf6f_2: first AppWorld call was `import apis.api_docs as api_docs`; rejected with the same bare block; agent then probed globals instead of calling the pre-injected object.
34d9492_2: agent executed `import apis.api_docs as docs`; tool returned `Usage of the following module is not allowed: apis.`; no file_system discovery or completion followed.
3c13f5a_1: two blocked `import apis.api_docs` attempts, then max-turn termination; prompt/tool text resembled a module path but never said `apis` was pre-injected or forbidden to import.
3c13f5a_2: blocked imports followed by blocked `os.listdir`, no task progress; rejection message was a bare traceback with no recovery guidance.
manifest.root_cause: The `apis` execution contract was not explicit and the sandbox's import rejection was not actionable. The tool description and prompt exposed `apis.api_docs...` syntax without stating that `apis` is a pre-injected global that must be called directly and must not be imported, so agents opened with `import apis...`, got a bare `Usage of the following module is not allowed: apis.` traceback, and burned turns retrying until the 30-turn cap terminated the run.
manifest.targeted_fix: Made the execution contract explicit in the MCP tool description and added a root CLAUDE.md that says `apis` is pre-injected, must be called directly, and must not be imported. In `servers/appworld.py`, wrapped AppWorld execute responses so any blocked-module rejection gets an appended actionable hint: remove the `import apis...` statement and call `apis.<service>.<api>()` directly. This generalizes to all tasks and does not hard-code any task answer.

failure_evidence: 3c13f5a_2: assistant issued three parallel appworld_execute calls (call_00 app docs, call_01 file_system docs, call_02 venmo docs); only call_00 got a ToolResultBlock, and call_01/call_02 were never answered, denying the agent required API schemas.

07b42fd_1, 22cc237_1, 29caf6f_3, 2a163ab_1, 302c169_3, 60d0b5b_1, 6104387_2, 692c77d_1: rollouts end during/after show_app_descriptions/show_api_descriptions discovery with no supervisor.complete_task call and no world-state mutation.
07b42fd_1, 22cc237_2, 29caf6f_3, 60d0b5b_1, 6104387_2: supplied tool-result evidence is truncated mid-JSON/API listing, so clipped output is indistinguishable from a clean early stop.
manifest.root_cause: The AppWorld MCP bridge did not guarantee one result per tool call (JSON-RPC batch requests were silently discarded) and read sidecar responses with StreamReader.readline() under a hard buffer limit, so large API-doc outputs could be clipped or fail. The harness also had no termination gate: rollouts could end after read-only discovery without calling supervisor.complete_task, and nothing forced the agent to continue.
manifest.targeted_fix: Hardened servers/appworld.py to answer every request exactly once (including JSON-RPC batches), read full newline-delimited sidecar responses, add explicit timeout/truncation markers, and isolate per-request errors. Added a fail-open Stop hook that blocks early termination until an actual supervisor.complete_task invocation appears in the transcript. Extended CLAUDE.md with the completion/state-change contract and targeted API-discovery guidance.

failure_evidence: 29caf6f_2, 2a163ab_2, 2a163ab_3, 302c169_1, 6104387_1, 76f2c72_1, afc0fce_2 stop after read-only API discovery (or zero tool calls) with no mutating call and no supervisor.complete_task; error_message is null and the AppWorld MCP server is connected.

3c13f5a_3, b0a8eae_1, b0a8eae_2 hit the 30-turn cap after early discovery with no completion; stderr shows generate_session_title [claude-code:unrecognized_model] for deepseek-flash, but the supplied traces do not prove that caused the exhaustion.
All supplied traces are truncated or missing later actions, so the early-stop conclusions are provisional.
The bundled Claude Code SDK does not set stop_hook_active for plugin Stop hooks (the CLI defaults it to false), and the existing hook treated that as an automatic approve.
manifest.root_cause: The Stop-hook completion guard was gated on stop_hook_active, but the Claude Code SDK does not propagate stop_hook_active to plugin Stop hooks, so the hook approved every no-completion stop and rollouts ended after discovery. Oversized show_app_descriptions/show_api_doc outputs and CLAUDE.md guidance that did not force narrow re-query or date lookup compounded the stalls.
manifest.targeted_fix: Made the Stop hook block any evidenced no-completion stop regardless of stop_hook_active (with last_assistant_message fallback and fail-open only when no evidence is available), bounded and explicitly flagged large AppWorld outputs in the MCP bridge, reinforced CLAUDE.md completion/discovery/date guidance, and raised the CLI Stop-hook block cap to match the 30-turn budget.

failure_evidence: 07b42fd_1, 6104387_3, 2a163ab_1, 76f2c72_2, and 76f2c72_3 show read-only AppWorld discovery only, no world-state mutation, and no supervisor.complete_task call; several are cut mid-JSON inside oversized API-doc output.
7d7fbf6_3 batched four show_api_doc results into one oversized result that was truncated before the agent could act on it.
22cc237_2, 22cc237_3, 302c169_2, and 76f2c72_1 hit the 30-turn cap after discovery; their stderr tail shows [claude-code:unrecognized_model] deepseek-flash for generate_session_title.
302c169_2 additionally hit a 401 on phone.show_alarms() and did not attempt the phone login API.
All supplied traces lack observable state mutation plus supervisor.complete_task, which is the direct AppWorld pass/fail mechanism.
manifest.root_cause: The harness returned large, mostly low-signal discovery output that bloated or truncated context, and it did not actively push the agent from read-only discovery to state-changing calls. The Stop guard only blocked a terminal turn when a transcript was available and had no complete_task call, but it did not distinguish no-mutation stalls or fail-open evidence gaps. Separately, an auxiliary generate_session_title query used an unrecognized model alias and polluted stderr/context.
manifest.targeted_fix: Add tool-level progress, auth, and discovery-compaction guidance in the AppWorld MCP bridge; strengthen the Stop hook to block no-mutation transcripts and read nested assistant text; disable nonessential Claude Code housekeeping traffic; and document the auth-recovery and task_completed=false rules in the prompt.

manifest.root_cause: The harness correctly reported task_completed:false after read-only calls, but it emitted one non-escalating repeated warning, never named the answer/QA terminal route, and did not flag malformed or truncated AppWorld results. Agents therefore stalled in discovery or stopped without the required completion call. b0a8eae_1 additionally shows missing model/config validation, which is outside the editable plugin files.
manifest.targeted_fix: Made the MCP bridge stateful with escalating read-only-streak nudges and task-type-aware completion guidance; added detection/recovery hints for malformed and truncated AppWorld payloads and printed dumps; updated the Stop-hook block reason to name complete_task(answer=...) for answer/QA tasks; and expanded CLAUDE.md with terminal-action and anti-stall rules plus a no-batching rule for full-schema prints.
